AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The aim of this study was to examine prevalence of obesity (body mass index of 30 or higher), no leisure-time physical activity in the past 30 days (no LTPA), and short sleep duration (averaging less than 7 hours of sleep per 24-hour period) among 22 occupational groups.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We analyzed 2013 and 2014 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) data from 29 states, controlling for sex, age, race/ethnicity, and education.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: By occupation, prevalence ranged from 16.1% to 35.8% for obesity, 11.3% to 28.7% for no LTPA, and 31.4% to 42.9% for short sleep. Only Transportation & Material Moving ranked among the top five occupations for all three risk factors. Obesity and no LTPA varied significantly by sex for several occupations.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Prevalence of obesity, no LTPA, and short sleep varied by occupation and affected more than one in five U.S. workers.
